findings.description: I-011 is not covered. design.md:5 says the integration items hold at this wave's merge for the components that exist by then. I-011 (00.design.md:687) says: 'The default values in docs/api/defaults.md SHALL equal the defaults in the configuration classes, checked by a test.' RouterPolicy is a configuration class that exists at the wave 3 merge. defaults.md:40 '| `TRACE`, `CONNECT` 메서드 | 라우팅 안 함 | 명시 정책 (**(미확정)**) |' documents its default. OPS-HTTP-001 AC-6 edits that row, but no AC checks that the documented default ('라우팅 안 함') equals RouterPolicy's default (enableTrace()/enableConnect() false on RouterPolicy.builder().build() / strict()). No requirement in 04.http-core.srs.md cites I-011.
findings.evidence: 00.design.md:687 [I-011]; docs/api/defaults.md:40; OPS-HTTP-001 AC-6 'docs/api/defaults.md names app.routerPolicy(...) with enableTrace/enableConnect as the explicit TRACE/CONNECT policy'; grep 'I-011' docs/spec/*.md -> no hit
findings.suggested_fix: Add to OPS-HTTP-001 AC-6: 'and a test checks that the default of that row (TRACE and CONNECT not routed) equals RouterPolicy.builder().build().enableTrace() == false and enableConnect() == false [I-011]'.

findings.description: The method template has 'app (RestApp), req (Request) and res (Response) in scope'. If req and res are method parameters or locals, a block with a `(req, res) -> ...` lambda does not compile, because a lambda parameter cannot redeclare a local in the enclosing scope. The examples wave 3 must add are likely written that way: the stream example of AC-3 and the routerPolicy examples of AC-4/AC-5. Fields of the enclosing class avoid the clash, so the AC can be met, but the text does not say which to use.
findings.evidence: AC-9 '...placed in a method template that declares `throws Exception`, has `app` (`RestApp`), `req` (`Request`) and `res` (`Response`) in scope...'; routing.md block 2 'app.route(Method.get().post().delete(), "/users/:id", (req, res) -> {'
findings.suggested_fix: Say that app, req and res are fields of the template class (an instance method template, so `this`-free stubs and lambdas named req/res compile).

findings.description: 'D-072 is met by the wave 1 convention: package com.snoworca.naruserve is annotated JSpecify @NullMarked'. The @NullMarked package annotation is not from wave 1. Wave 1 (CON-BUILD-011) annotated each method explicitly (NullabilityFixture: '@Nullable String annotatedNullable()', '@NonNull String annotatedNonNull()'). The package-info.java that carries @NullMarked is tagged '// @req IR-ROUTE-003', which is wave 2. The rule works, but the AC names the wrong source for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'the wave 1 convention' with 'the wave 2 package convention (JSpecify of CON-BUILD-011, @NullMarked package as in com.snoworca.naruserve.routing)'.

findings.description: I-003 ('The public API of NaruServe-api MUST NOT expose java.nio.file, CompletableFuture or java.net.http types') is checked only for the SPI (CON-HTTP-001 AC-1). Wave 3 adds most of the public API (Request, Response, RestApp, RouteBuilder, RouteHandler, BodyAlreadyConsumedException), and no AC checks these types. No wave 1 or wave 2 check covers I-003 either (grep I-003 docs/spec -> no hit). The current design makes this easy to meet, but no test traces it at the merge.
findings.evidence: 00.design.md:676 [I-003]; CON-HTTP-001 AC-1 '...Every type of the HttpAdapter SPI ... signatures reference only java.* types (excluding java.nio.file.*, ...CompletableFuture and java.net.http.*)'
findings.suggested_fix: Widen CON-HTTP-001 AC-1, or the reflection tests of IR-HTTP-001 AC-4 and IR-HTTP-005 AC-5, to cover every public type in com.snoworca.naruserve [I-003].

findings.description: The in-memory adapter binds, runs the drain loop on 'an adapter-chosen thread' and has 'adapter threads' that the final release waits for. I-015 ('Every test that starts a server SHALL assert after shutdown that no server thread ... remains') is not stated for these bind/stop tests. Whether the in-memory adapter counts as a server is open, but the final-release AC never asserts that its threads are gone.
findings.evidence: 00.design.md:695 [I-015]; IR-HTTP-004 AC-4 'a separate final release that waits at most a fixed margin for the adapter's threads to end; the in-memory adapter implements both and a test shows an in-flight exchange still running at the deadline is force-closed'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC-4: 'and after the final release the test finds no thread the in-memory adapter started still alive [I-015]'.

findings.description: Both requirements still depend only on the discarded CON-ROUTE-001 ('Requirement | CON-ROUTE-001 | depends_on'), and neither has a depends_on row to its successor CON-ROUTE-006. Rows cannot be removed, but a successor row can be added.
findings.evidence: 04.http-core.srs.md IR-HTTP-002 trace 'CON-ROUTE-001 | depends_on | RouteHandler is the router handler type'; CON-HTTP-001 trace 'CON-ROUTE-001 | depends_on | same engine-free rule as the router'
findings.suggested_fix: add_trace_link Requirement CON-ROUTE-006 depends_on on both.

findings.description: The AC says 'the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding', but the carried rule says 'the validator does not decode' (carried-into-wave-3.md). PathValidator does decode each segment internally to find an encoded '/' or '..'; it just never returns a decoded path. The meaning is clear from the example, but the wording conflicts with the carried bullet.
findings.evidence: FR-HTTP-002 AC-3; carried-into-wave-3.md 'the validator does not decode'; PathValidator.java 'It answers accept or reject only; it never returns a decoded path.'
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'the validator receives the raw path undecoded and checks each segment after one percent-decoding'.
